def TrainTextModel(numEpochs,batchSize,lr,seed,maxPages,dataDir,source="pages",resume=False,
                   warmStart=None,personalFraction=0.20,tag=None):
    personalSet = personalVal = None
    if source=="joint":
        trainSet,personalSet,valSet,personalVal = BuildJointSplit(dataDir)
    elif source=="teklia":
        trainSet,valSet = BuildTekliaSplit(dataDir)
    else:
        trainSet,valSet = BuildPagesSplit(maxPages,dataDir)
    print(f"[Split] Train lines: {len(trainSet)} | Held-out val lines: {len(valSet)}")

    numClasses = len(CHARSET)+1
    params = InitTextModelParams(seed,numClasses)
    trainable = TrainableParams(params)
    optimizer = RMSprop(trainable,lr=lr,weightDecay=1e-5)
    scheduler = ReduceLrOnPlateau(optimizer,factor=0.5,patience=5,minLr=1e-5)

    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    bestValLoss = np.inf
    bestPath = WEIGHTS_DIR/"paper_cnn_bilstm_ctc_scratch_best.npz"
    ckptPath = WEIGHTS_DIR/"paper_cnn_bilstm_ctc_scratch_checkpoint.npz"
    logPath = WEIGHTS_DIR/"paper_cnn_bilstm_ctc_scratch_log.txt"

    startEpoch = 1
    if warmStart:
        loaded = LoadParamsInto(params,warmStart)
        print(f"[WarmStart] loaded {loaded}/{len(params)} tensors from {warmStart}")
    if resume and ckptPath.exists():
        loaded = LoadParamsInto(params,ckptPath)
        prevEpoch,prevBest = LoadCheckpointMeta(ckptPath)
        startEpoch = prevEpoch+1
        if prevBest is not None:
            bestValLoss = prevBest
        print(f"[Resume] loaded {loaded}/{len(params)} tensors from {ckptPath}, "
              f"continuing at epoch {startEpoch} (best val loss so far {bestValLoss:.4f})")

    for epoch in range(startEpoch,startEpoch+numEpochs):
        epochStart = time.time()
        epochLoss,nBatches = 0.0,0
        batches = (IterateMixedBatches(trainSet,personalSet,batchSize,personalFraction,rng)
                   if personalSet is not None
                   else IterateBatches(trainSet,batchSize,rng,shuffle=True))
        for batch in batches:
            images,targets,_texts = TextNumpyBatch(batch)
            rawLogits,cache = TextModelForward(images,params)
            loss,dRawLogits = CtcLoss(rawLogits,targets)
            _,grads = TextModelBackward(dRawLogits,cache)
            trainableGrads = {k:grads[k] for k in trainable}
            optimizer.Step(trainableGrads)
            epochLoss+=loss
            nBatches+=1
            if nBatches==1 or nBatches%5==0:
                print(f"\r[TrainText] Epoch {epoch:03d} | Batch {nBatches:04d} | "
                      f"Running loss {epochLoss/nBatches:.3f}",end="",flush=True)
        print()
        trainLoss = epochLoss/max(1,nBatches)

        valLoss,valCharAcc = ValidateTextModel(valSet,params,batchSize,rng)
        if personalVal is not None and len(personalVal):
            #the public held-out set says whether it reads handwriting, this
            #one says whether it reads these writers
            _pLoss,pAcc = ValidateTextModel(personalVal,params,batchSize,rng)
            print(f"[TrainText] held-out personal char-acc {pAcc:.2%}")
        scheduler.Step(valLoss)
        improved = valLoss<bestValLoss
        savedMsg = ""
        if improved:
            bestValLoss = valLoss
            SaveCheckpoint(bestPath,params,extra={"__epoch__":np.array(epoch),"__best__":np.array(bestValLoss)})
            savedMsg = " [BEST SAVED]"
        SaveCheckpoint(ckptPath,params,extra={"__epoch__":np.array(epoch),"__best__":np.array(bestValLoss)})

        elapsedMin = (time.time()-epochStart)/60
        print(f"[TrainText] Epoch {epoch:03d} | Train loss {trainLoss:.3f} | "
              f"Val loss {valLoss:.3f} (best {bestValLoss:.3f}) | Val char-acc {valCharAcc:.2%} | "
              f"lr {optimizer.lr:.6f} | {elapsedMin:.1f} min{savedMsg}")
        AppendLog(logPath,f"epoch={epoch} train_loss={trainLoss:.4f} val_loss={valLoss:.4f} "
                          f"best_val_loss={bestValLoss:.4f} val_char_acc={valCharAcc:.4f} "
                          f"lr={optimizer.lr:.6f} minutes={elapsedMin:.1f}{savedMsg}")

    return bestValLoss

def AuthorModelForward(x,params,training,rng):
    backboneOut,backboneCache = BackboneForwardTrain(x,params)
    pooledH,hpCache = AdaptiveMaxPoolHeightForward(backboneOut)
    squeezed = pooledH[:,:,0,:]
    pooledW,apCache = AdaptiveAvgPoolWidthForward(squeezed)   #the width is collapsed too
    pooled = pooledW[:,:,0]

    h,lin1Cache = LinearForward(pooled,params["author_head.0.weight"],params["author_head.0.bias"])
    h,reluCache = ReluForward(h)
    h,dropCache = DropoutForward(h,0.2,training,rng)
    logits,lin2Cache = LinearForward(h,params["author_head.3.weight"],params["author_head.3.bias"])

    cache = dict(backboneCache=backboneCache,hpCache=hpCache,apCache=apCache,
                 lin1Cache=lin1Cache,reluCache=reluCache,dropCache=dropCache,lin2Cache=lin2Cache)
    return logits,cache
inventory.comment: AuthorModelForward: the namer forward, backbone, pooling over height and width, one score per writer

def AuthorModelBackward(dLogits,cache):
    grads = {}
    dh,dw2,db2 = LinearBackward(dLogits,cache["lin2Cache"])
    grads["author_head.3.weight"] = dw2
    grads["author_head.3.bias"] = db2

    dh = DropoutBackward(dh,cache["dropCache"])
    dh = ReluBackward(dh,cache["reluCache"])
    dpooled,dw1,db1 = LinearBackward(dh,cache["lin1Cache"])
    grads["author_head.0.weight"] = dw1
    grads["author_head.0.bias"] = db1

    dPooledW = dpooled[:,:,None]
    dSqueezed = AdaptiveAvgPoolWidthBackward(dPooledW,cache["apCache"])
    dPooledH = dSqueezed[:,:,None,:]
    dBackboneOut = AdaptiveMaxPoolHeightBackward(dPooledH,cache["hpCache"])
    dx,backboneGrads = BackboneBackwardTrain(dBackboneOut,cache["backboneCache"])
    grads.update(backboneGrads)
    return dx,grads
inventory.comment: ---AuthorModelBackward: and back again---

def TrainAuthorModel(numEpochs,batchSize,lr,seed,resume=False,warmStart=None,
                     writers=None):
    #the writer list is passed in, leaving paths.py untouched
    wanted = list(writers) if writers else list(paths.DatabaseWriters+paths.PersonalWriters)
    unknown = [w for w in wanted if w not in paths.DatabaseWriters+paths.PersonalWriters]
    if unknown:
        raise SystemExit("unknown writer(s): %s\nknown: %s"
                         % (", ".join(unknown),
                            ", ".join(paths.DatabaseWriters+paths.PersonalWriters)))
    wantedDb = [w for w in paths.DatabaseWriters if w in wanted]

    base = IAMLineDatasetRaw(rootDir=str(DEFAULT_AUTHOR_DATA_DIR),cacheDir=str(DEFAULT_AUTHOR_CACHE_DIR))
    before = len(base.samples)
    base.samples = [s for s in base.samples if s["page_key"].split("/")[0] in wantedDb]
    print(f"[Filter] kept {len(base.samples)}/{before} database samples for {wantedDb}")

    AddPersonalSamples(base)
    #the writers left out are dropped before the split, or one could still
    #land in validation and be scored against a class the model has not got
    base.samples = [s for s in base.samples if s["page_key"].split("/")[0] in wanted]
    base.authorFolders = sorted(wanted)
    base.authorToIdx = {a:i for i,a in enumerate(base.authorFolders)}
    print(f"[Authors] {len(base.authorFolders)}: {base.authorFolders}")
    print(f"[Crops] stroke-normalised at {CLS.PenWidthXh:.2f} x-heights")

    trainIdx,valIdx = base.HoldoutSplitIndices()
    if not valIdx:
        raise RuntimeError("No holdout lines found.")
    trainSet = AuthorLabeledView(base,trainIdx,isTrain=True)
    valSet = AuthorLabeledView(base,valIdx,isTrain=False)
    print(f"[Split] Train lines: {len(trainIdx)} | Held-out val lines: {len(valIdx)}")

    numAuthors = len(base.authorFolders)
    params = InitAuthorModelParams(seed,numAuthors)
    trainable = TrainableParams(params)
    optimizer = AdamW(trainable,lr=lr,weightDecay=1e-4)
    scheduler = CosineAnnealingLr(optimizer,tMax=numEpochs)

    rngBatch = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    rngDropout = np.random.default_rng(seed+1)
    bestAcc = 0.0
    stem = "author_shape_11w_pw170_scratch"
    outPath = WEIGHTS_DIR/(stem+"_weights.npz")
    ckptPath = WEIGHTS_DIR/(stem+"_checkpoint.npz")
    logPath = WEIGHTS_DIR/(stem+"_log.txt")
    print(f"[Output] {outPath.name}")

    startEpoch = 1
    if warmStart:
        loaded = LoadParamsInto(params,warmStart)
        print(f"[WarmStart] loaded {loaded}/{len(params)} tensors from {warmStart}")
    if resume and ckptPath.exists():
        loaded = LoadParamsInto(params,ckptPath)
        prevEpoch,prevBest = LoadCheckpointMeta(ckptPath)
        startEpoch = prevEpoch+1
        if prevBest is not None:
            bestAcc = prevBest
        print(f"[Resume] loaded {loaded}/{len(params)} tensors from {ckptPath}, "
              f"continuing at epoch {startEpoch} (best val acc so far {bestAcc:.3f})")

    for epoch in range(startEpoch,startEpoch+numEpochs):
        epochStart = time.time()
        epochLoss,nBatches = 0.0,0
        for batch in IterateBatches(trainSet,batchSize,rngBatch,shuffle=True):
            images,authorIdxs,_ = AuthorCollateFn(batch)
            logits,cache = AuthorModelForward(images,params,training=True,rng=rngDropout)
            loss,dLogits = CrossEntropyLoss(logits,authorIdxs)
            _,grads = AuthorModelBackward(dLogits,cache)
            trainableGrads = {k:grads[k] for k in trainable}
            ClipGradNorm(trainableGrads,maxNorm=5.0)
            optimizer.Step(trainableGrads)
            epochLoss+=loss
            nBatches+=1
        scheduler.Step()
        trainLoss = epochLoss/max(1,nBatches)

        valAcc = ValidateAuthorModel(valSet,params,batchSize,rngBatch)
        savedMsg = ""
        if valAcc>bestAcc:
            bestAcc = valAcc
            SaveCheckpoint(outPath,params,extra={"__author_names__":np.array(base.authorFolders),
                                                  "__epoch__":np.array(epoch),"__best__":np.array(bestAcc)})
            savedMsg = " [SAVED]"
        SaveCheckpoint(ckptPath,params,extra={"__author_names__":np.array(base.authorFolders),
                                               "__epoch__":np.array(epoch),"__best__":np.array(bestAcc)})

        elapsedMin = (time.time()-epochStart)/60
        print(f"[TrainAuthor] Epoch {epoch:03d} | loss {trainLoss:.3f} | val author-acc {valAcc:.3f} "
              f"(best {bestAcc:.3f}) | lr {optimizer.lr:.6f} | {elapsedMin:.1f} min{savedMsg}")
        AppendLog(logPath,f"epoch={epoch} train_loss={trainLoss:.4f} val_acc={valAcc:.4f} "
                          f"best_val_acc={bestAcc:.4f} lr={optimizer.lr:.6f} minutes={elapsedMin:.1f}")

    print(f"\nBest val author-accuracy: {bestAcc:.3f}")
    print(f"Weights saved to: {outPath}")
    return bestAcc
inventory.comment: TrainAuthorModel: the namer's training run, the same shape of loop with cross entropy instead of CTC.  every crop is stroke-normalised first, the same preparation ClassifyImage applies at inference

def Main():
    import argparse
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="train the reader or the namer from first principles")

                         "database pages here")

def PreviewStart(index=None):
    import cv2
    global _previewCap
    with _GetLock():
        if _previewCap is not None:
            return
        idx = CAMERA_INDEX if index is None else index
        cap = cv2.VideoCapture(idx)
        if not cap.isOpened():
            cap.release()
            raise RuntimeError(f"Could not open camera at index {idx} for preview.")
        _previewCap = cap

def _CapThreads():
    for v in ("OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "OMP_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS"):
        os.environ[v] = "1"
    try:
        import ctypes
        import glob
        import numpy
        root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(numpy.__file__)))
        pats = [os.path.join(root, "numpy.libs", "*openblas*.so*"),
                os.path.join(root, "numpy", ".libs", "*openblas*.so*")]
        #the wheel renames its symbols, so the plain name is not there: the
        #board carries libscipy_openblas64_, whose entry point is
        #scipy_openblas_set_num_threads64_.  every spelling seen in the
        #numpy and scipy builds is tried in turn
        names = ("scipy_openblas_set_num_threads64_",
                 "scipy_openblas_set_num_threads_64_",
                 "scipy_openblas_set_num_threads",
                 "openblas_set_num_threads64_",
                 "openblas_set_num_threads",
                 "scipy_goto_set_num_threads64_",
                 "goto_set_num_threads")
        for pat in pats:
            for so in glob.glob(pat):
                lib = ctypes.CDLL(so)
                for fn in names:
                    if hasattr(lib, fn):
                        getattr(lib, fn)(1)
                        return True
    except Exception:
        pass
    return False
inventory.comment: _CapThreads: one maths-library thread per worker six workers each asking the library for six threads would put 36 threads on six cores and spend the gain on contention.  the environment variables are read when the library loads, which has already happened in the parent, so the live setting is changed through the library itself where that entry point can be found, and the variables are set as well for any library loaded later

def OpenUpright(src):
    """Open an image with its EXIF orientation applied to the pixels.

    A phone or webcam does not usually turn the sensor frame round when the
    camera is held sideways.  It writes the pixels as the sensor read them
    and records a separate orientation tag saying how far to turn them.
    Every viewer honours that tag, so the file LOOKS upright, but PIL hands
    back the raw pixels and ignores it, so the segmenter was reading a page
    lying on its side while the same file looked correct on screen.

    That is not a small error.  A sideways page makes the horizontal
    projection cut ACROSS the writing instead of between the lines, so the
    segmenter returned about forty narrow vertical slices of text and the
    recogniser read gibberish from them.  Measured on the nine photographed
    gantry pages: 5.7 per cent mean character accuracy before this call,
    65.1 per cent after it, best page 90.2 per cent.

    exif_transpose is a no-op on a file with no orientation tag, which is
    what cv2.imwrite produces for the webcam captures, so this is safe to
    use on every path into the system.
    """
    return ImageOps.exif_transpose(Image.open(src))

inventory.name: ReadAllLines
inventory.source:
def ReadAllLines(crops):
    """Read every crop, and settle which end of the page is up.

    The axis test cannot tell a page from the same page turned through
    180 degrees, because the rows of writing fall in the same places
    either way.  The reader can.  Turning the page over is the same as
    turning every crop over and reversing their order, so it is read both
    ways here and whichever the reader is more confident of wins.  That
    needs no second segmentation.

    Only a SAMPLE of lines is read both ways.  Reading every line twice
    settled it too, and identically on the test page, but it put the read
    stage up from 5.9 s to 11.9 s on a sixteen line page, which is most
    of the per character allowance spent proving something three lines
    already show beyond doubt.  The sampled lines are not read again.
    """
    def Read(c, flip):
        img = np.rot90(c, 2) if flip else c
        return REC.ReadTextScored(Image.fromarray(img).convert("L"), TEXT_MODEL)

    n = len(crops)
    probe = list(np.unique(np.linspace(0, n-1, min(ORIENT_PROBE_LINES, n))
                           .round().astype(int)))
    fwd = {i: Read(crops[i], False) for i in probe}
    rev = {i: Read(crops[i], True) for i in probe}
    sF = float(np.mean([fwd[i][1] for i in probe]))
    sR = float(np.mean([rev[i][1] for i in probe]))

    flip = sR > sF
    cache = rev if flip else fwd
    #the probed lines are already read; the rest are independent of one
    #another and go out to the pool
    todo = [(i, crops[i], flip) for i in range(n) if i not in cache]
    done = {i: (t, sc) for i, t, sc in LW.Map(LW.ReadOne, todo)}
    out = [cache[i] if i in cache else done[i] for i in range(n)]
    if flip:
        #the order the lines come back in changes too, so the caller is
        #given it and can put everything else it holds per line in step
        idx = list(range(n))[::-1]
        return ([np.rot90(crops[i], 2) for i in idx], [out[i][0] for i in idx],
                [out[i][1] for i in idx], idx, 180, sF, sR)
    idx = list(range(n))
    return (list(crops), [t for t, _s in out], [s for _t, s in out], idx, 0, sF, sR)

inventory.name: NameWriter
inventory.source:
def NameWriter(crops):
    """One writer for the page, from every line, weighted by ink.

    Two changes from naming off six lines spread down the page.

    The six were picked with linspace, which always includes the LAST
    index, so a junk crop at the foot of the page got a vote in every
    pool and at two lines was half of it.  On the page that prompted
    this, every one of the sixteen real lines named the writer correctly
    on its own, yet the pooled confidence came back at 78.4 per cent
    because the seventeenth crop was a blot.  Dropping the blots is the
    first half of the fix; letting every surviving line vote, so that no
    single crop can carry that much weight, is the second.

    The vote is then weighted by how much ink the line carries.  On that
    same page the per line confidence ran from 48.4 to 100 per cent, and
    the three weakest lines were the three shortest ones: two words of
    writing is less evidence than a full line and should not count the
    same as one.
    """
    got = LW.Map(LW.NameOne, [(i, c) for i, c in enumerate(crops)])
    per = [p for _i, p in sorted(got, key=lambda r: r[0])]
    w = np.array([float((c < 128).sum()) for c in crops], dtype=np.float64)
    if w.sum() <= 0:
        w = np.ones(len(crops), dtype=np.float64)
    avg = (np.vstack(per)*w[:, None]).sum(axis=0)/w.sum()
    return per, avg, w

def SplitExpected(expectedText, n):
    """Per line truth, but only when the expected text really is per line.

    If the user pasted a paragraph, there is no honest way to say which
    written line each word belongs to, so this returns None and the per
    line accuracy columns are left empty rather than guessed at.
    """
    got = [l.strip() for l in (expectedText or "").splitlines() if l.strip()]
    return got if len(got) == n and n > 0 else None

def ApiClassify():
    expectedText = (request.form.get("expected_text") or "").strip()
    expectedAuthor = request.form.get("expected_author") or ""

    run = TIMING.Run("classify")
    with run.Step("loading", chars=0):
        if "image" in request.files and request.files["image"].filename:
            #OpenUpright, not Image.open: an uploaded photograph carries its
            #orientation in EXIF, and the saved copy below is what the page
            #and the segmenter both read afterwards, so it is turned ONCE
            #here and the two can never disagree
            page = OpenUpright(request.files["image"].stream).convert("L")
            imageId = uuid.uuid4().hex
        elif request.form.get("image_id"):
            imageId = "".join(c for c in request.form["image_id"] if c.isalnum())
            p = UPLOADS/("%s.jpg" % imageId)
            if not p.exists():
                return jsonify({"error": "Unknown image_id"}), 400
            page = Image.open(p).convert("L")
        else:
            return jsonify({"error": "Provide either 'image' or 'image_id'"}), 400
        #stood on its correct axis HERE, however it arrived, and the copy
        #saved to disk is the stood up one, so the picture the browser
        #shows and the one the segmenter reads stay the same picture.  an
        #already upright page scores higher on its own axis and is left be
        gray, axisDeg, axisScores = StandUp(np.asarray(page, dtype=np.uint8))
        Image.fromarray(gray).convert("RGB").save(UPLOADS/("%s.jpg" % imageId))

    #this tree's SegmentLines takes no timer, so conditioning, segmenting and
    #cropping cannot be reported apart here and the whole of it is one stage
    with run.Step("segmenting", chars=0):
        lines, _dbg, info = SEG.SegmentLines(gray)
    crops = [np.asarray(ln["image"]) for ln in lines]
    if not crops:
        return jsonify({"error": "No handwriting lines were detected.",
                        "timing": Remember(run)}), 422

    with run.Step("reading", chars=0) as step:
        crops, readLines, readScores, order, flipDeg, sF, sR = ReadAllLines(crops)
        lines = [lines[i] for i in order]   #keep the crop metadata in step
        step.chars = sum(len(t) for t in readLines)
    predictedText = " ".join(readLines)

    with run.Step("naming", chars=len(predictedText)):
        perLineProbs, avg, inkWeights = NameWriter(crops)
        bestIdx = int(np.argmax(avg))
        predictedAuthor = PAGE_BY_INDEX[bestIdx]

    #---the per line table, which is what the downloadable report holds---
    truthLines = SplitExpected(expectedText, len(crops))
    named = [PAGE_BY_INDEX[int(np.argmax(p))] for p in perLineProbs]
    agree = sum(1 for n in named if n == predictedAuthor)
    correct = (sum(1 for n in named if n == expectedAuthor)
               if expectedAuthor else None)

    lineRows = []
    for i, p in enumerate(perLineProbs):
        t = truthLines[i] if truthLines else None
        lineRows.append({
            "line": i+1,
            "author_named": named[i],
            "author_confidence_pct": round(100*float(p[int(np.argmax(p))]), 1),
            "page_author_probability_pct": round(100*float(p[bestIdx]), 1),
            "author_matches_page": named[i] == predictedAuthor,
            "author_correct": (named[i] == expectedAuthor) if expectedAuthor else None,
            "char_accuracy_pct": (round(100*REC.CharAcc(readLines[i], t), 1)
                                  if t is not None else None),
            "word_accuracy_pct": (round(100*WordAcc(readLines[i], t), 1)
                                  if t is not None else None),
            "read_confidence": round(readScores[i], 3),
            "ink_pct": round(float(lines[i].get("inkPct", 0.0)), 2),
            "text_read": readLines[i],
            "text_expected": t,
        })

    meanLineChar = ([r["char_accuracy_pct"] for r in lineRows] if truthLines else None)
    run.chars = len(predictedText)
    run.lines = len(crops)

    payload = {
        "image_id": imageId,
        "predicted_text": predictedText,
        "predicted_lines": readLines,
        "text_accuracy_pct": (round(100*REC.CharAcc(predictedText, expectedText), 1)
                              if expectedText else None),
        "word_accuracy_pct": (round(100*WordAcc(predictedText, expectedText), 1)
                              if expectedText else None),
        #the mean of the per line figures, which is the one quoted per page
        "mean_line_char_accuracy_pct": (round(float(np.mean(meanLineChar)), 1)
                                        if meanLineChar else None),
        "predicted_author": predictedAuthor,
        #the pooled posterior over every line, weighted by ink
        "author_confidence_pct": round(100*float(avg[bestIdx]), 1),
        #and how many lines would have said so entirely on their own
        "author_line_agreement_pct": round(100.0*agree/len(crops), 1),
        "author_lines_agreeing": "%d/%d" % (agree, len(crops)),
        "author_line_correct_pct": (round(100.0*correct/len(crops), 1)
                                    if correct is not None else None),
        "author_correct": (predictedAuthor == expectedAuthor) if expectedAuthor else None,
        "lines_detected": len(crops),
        "lines_dropped_as_blots": info.get("dropped", 0),
        "orientation_applied_deg": (axisDeg+flipDeg) % 360,
        "orientation_scores": dict(axisScores, read_upright=round(sF, 3),
                                   read_inverted=round(sR, 3)),
        "page_angle_deg": info.get("angle"),
        "line_pitch_px": info.get("pitch"),
        "per_author_confidence_pct": {PAGE_BY_INDEX[i]: round(100*float(v), 1)
                                      for i, v in enumerate(avg)},
        "lines": lineRows,
        "timing": Remember(run),
    }
    payload["report_url"] = WriteReport(imageId, payload)
    return jsonify(payload)

inventory.name: ReadBackText
inventory.source:
def ReadBackText(previewImg, pxPerMm):
    """Read a rendered page back the way a photographed one is read.

    REC.ReadText is a LINE recogniser: it runs ResizeLineImageFixed, which
    squashes whatever it is given into a single strip a few dozen pixels
    tall.  Handing it a whole multi-line page crushes three lines of
    writing on top of each other, and it returns gibberish -- measured at
    24.1 per cent on a three line job that reads 83.0 per cent when the
    lines are taken one at a time.

    So the page goes through the same segmenter a photograph does.  Two
    details matter.  The render is cropped tight to the ink, and the
    segmenter needs paper around the writing to work: with no margin it
    clipped the first and last letters and scored 64.7 per cent against
    94.1 per cent once padded.  And a page that segments to a single line
    is read whole, because for one line the crop can only lose edges that
    the full image still has.
    """
    arr = np.asarray(previewImg, dtype=np.uint8)
    pad = max(8, int(8.0*float(pxPerMm or 8.0)))   #8 mm of paper, as the writers' own sheets have
    padded = np.full((arr.shape[0]+2*pad, arr.shape[1]+2*pad), 255, np.uint8)
    padded[pad:pad+arr.shape[0], pad:pad+arr.shape[1]] = arr
    try:
        #mergeValley is asked for HERE and nowhere else.  a rendered page is
        #drawn at one pen width with no paper behind it, and on that input a
        #single line's descender band is readily taken for a second line; the
        #merge fixes exactly that.  it is left off for photographs, where it
        #was measured to change nothing and cost 0.4 points
        lines, _dbg, _info = SEG.SegmentLines(padded, mergeValley=0.72)
    except Exception:
        #a read-back is a report, never the job: if segmenting throws, say
        #what the single-line path says rather than failing the request
        return REC.ReadText(previewImg, TEXT_MODEL)
    if len(lines) <= 1:
        return REC.ReadText(previewImg, TEXT_MODEL)
    return " ".join(filter(None, (
        REC.ReadText(Image.fromarray(np.asarray(ln["image"])).convert("L"), TEXT_MODEL)
        for ln in lines)))
inventory.comment: ====================================================================== WRITING TEXT IN A WRITER'S HAND the joint search draws nTries candidates and keeps whichever scores best on the harmonic mean of how readable it is and how much it looks like the requested writer, which is the selection that lifted both figures ======================================================================

def ApiGenerate():
    data = request.get_json(force=True) or {}
    text = (data.get("text") or "").strip()
    author = data.get("author")
    nTries = int(data.get("nTries", DEFAULT_TRIES))
    if not text:
        return jsonify({"error": "text is required"}), 400
    if author not in PROFILES:
        return jsonify({"error": "Unknown author %r" % author}), 400
    #a curated profile is the same hand with a tidier library, so the writer
    #model is asked about the writer, not about the file.  without this the
    #curated profiles appear in the author list and every one of them is
    #refused, because the classifier's classes are the plain names
    judged = BaseAuthor(author)
    if judged not in SHAPE_MAP:
        return jsonify({"error": "No writer model for %r, so its output cannot be "
                                 "judged during the search" % author}), 400

    profile = PROFILES[author]
    #which ruled line to write on.  without it every job lands at the same
    #height and the second one is drawn on top of the first
    cfg = REP.GantryConfig()
    lineH = float(data.get("lineHeightMm") or cfg.lineHeightMm)
    lineIdx = max(0, int(data.get("line", 0)))
    #the two feeds are separate because they buy different things.  the
    #pen-down feed is a quality control: a tight curve drawn too fast
    #overshoots, which is what rounds off the small loops of an 'e'.  the
    #pen-up feed is pure time, since nothing is being drawn while the
    #carriage crosses the page, so it can be raised to pay for a slower
    #draw without costing any accuracy.  clamped to what the runner will
    #accept at the bottom and to a rate the belts hold at the top
    drawFeed = _Clamp(data.get("drawFeedMmMin"), cfg.drawFeedMmMin, 60.0, 3000.0)
    travelFeed = _Clamp(data.get("travelFeedMmMin"), cfg.travelFeedMmMin, 60.0, 6000.0)

def ApiGcodeUpload():
    if "gcode" not in request.files or not request.files["gcode"].filename:

    expectedText = (request.form.get("expected_text") or "").strip()

    jobDir = JOBS/jobId
